summary: Machine-readable map from every Template_Plugin hook event to the Kiro mechanism, tier, and skill-instruction location that delivers its behavior in the Bootcamp_Power. Not a hook definition: the Hook_Installer installs only files matching hookDefinitionGlob, and this file is deliberately excluded by that glob.

assumptionDependentValues.note: Every value in this map that depends on an unverified assumption is a substitution the Transformation_Contract fills as this file is materialized, so it has exactly one home and correcting it is a one-line contract edit plus a rebuild rather than a hand-patched asset (R3 AC4). This file as authored is therefore pre-substitution content, exactly as ported content is.

values.field: events[write-gate].kiroMechanism.matcher, and the same hook's matcher in senzing-bootcamp-write-gate.json
values.authoredAsNote: The template's own PreToolUse matcher, which release 0.5.1 carries in hooks/hooks.json. The Kiro write-tool regex is written down once, as this set's replacement value in tools/bootcamp-transform/contract.yaml, and nowhere else in the authored tree.

The Hook_Installer reads the resolved value from this field, the same way it reads hookDefinitionGlob. It owns the vocabulary below and the workspace copy directory name; the contract owns the choice.

scriptsDirectory.summary: How the Hook_Installer resolves <ABSOLUTE_SCRIPTS_DIR>. Both strategies are implemented in the installer; the Transformation_Contract's scripts-dir-strategy set chooses between them, so flipping the fallback on after the Test_Checklist step 10 observation needs no installer edit and no hook asset edit.

strategies.appliesWhen: assumption A4 holds — a Power's skills/*/scripts/ files are materialized at a stable absolute path after install

strategies.resolvesTo: a copy of the ported script set inside the Workspace_Hooks_Directory, alongside the hook definitions
strategies.workspaceFilesWritten: the hook definitions plus the copied script set, every path disclosed before it is written and every path under the senzing-bootcamp- prefix so removal still deletes exactly what was written
strategies.appliesWhen: assumption A4 is observed FALSE — the in-Power scripts path is not stable, so a hook naming it would silently never fire

destinations.role: Tier 2 asset directory the Hook_Installer reads with explicit Bootcamper consent
Tier 3 forward compatibility; inert if Kiro does not load bundled hooks

placement.note: The definitions are authored once in sourceDirectory, which mirrors the first destination of the contract's kiro-hooks rule. The engine materializes the same content at both destinations; the source is never duplicated.

commandStringPolicy.validatorGuidance: Remove the two placeholder tokens from the command string before scanning for a redirection operator. The tokens are spelled with angle brackets, so a literal scan for < or > over an unresolved shipped asset reports the placeholders themselves. Scan the remainder, and scan the installer's resolved output in full.

noOpGuard.rule: Every ported hook script exits without acting when the probe file is absent from the workspace, so an installed hook set never affects an unrelated Kiro session.
noOpGuard.note: The guard lives in the ported script bodies. No substitution set in the Transformation_Contract touches it, so porting preserves it byte-for-byte. Tier 1 restates the same guard in senzing-bootcamp-tier1-session-lifecycle.md.

tiers.description: Every hook-enforced behavior is also stated as an instruction, so the complete bootcamp is delivered with zero hook definitions installed (R7 AC4).
Restores mechanical enforcement where Kiro has an equivalent trigger (R7 AC5, AC6).
Forward compatibility only; every behavior also reaches the Bootcamper through Tier 1 or Tier 2 (R7 AC12).

tier1InstructionFilesNote: Authored as kiro-owned content under the owning skill (bootcamp-onboarding), because the ported bootcamp skills come from the resolved Template_Release and are not hand-authored here. The engine materializes them at the Tier 3 destination as well (dev.kiro/hooks/tier1-instructions/), where they are inert; the paths above are the declared instruction locations.

tier1Activation.note: Tier 1 delivery depends on these files being read. The client-adaptation skill points at them whether or not the Bootcamper consents to the Tier 2 install, so declining hooks still yields the complete rule set.

events.behavior: On session start, read config/bootcamp_progress.json and resume from the recorded module, or start onboarding when no module is recorded.

kiroMechanism.notes: Direct equivalent. Exit-0 stdout is forwarded to the session context.

portedProseLocations.note: Design-declared Tier 1 placement in ported prose. The ported files come from the resolved Template_Release, so these paths are reinforcement, not the declared instruction location.

events.behavior: Watch each Bootcamper prompt for feedback about the bootcamp and run the feedback capture workflow, appending to docs/feedback/SENZING_BOOTCAMP_PLUGIN_FEEDBACK.md.

kiroMechanism.notes: Direct equivalent. Exit-0 stdout is forwarded to the session context.

portedProseLocations.note: The capture workflow itself is ported prose; the Tier 1 instruction points at it rather than restating its format.

events.residualGap: The script does not read a literal manifest path; plugin_version() builds one from joined path segments. The manifest-path substitution set repoints it to the Power's plugin.json at the Power root, replacing the .claude-plugin segment with the two parent levels the move from <pluginRoot>/scripts/ to skills/bootcamp-onboarding/scripts/ added. Behavior is unchanged.

events.behavior: Keep the recap checkpoint current on every turn, so recap material is never more than one turn behind.

kiroMechanism.notes: Direct equivalent. Also the carrier that bounds the loss from Kiro having no PreCompact trigger.

portedProseLocations.note: Design-declared Tier 1 placement in ported prose.

events.templateMatcherNote: Recorded as the template's two tool names rather than as its `fs_write|str_replace|fs_append` alternation string, because this file is pre-substitution content and the contract's tool-names set rewrites that exact alternation wherever it appears — including here, where the record of what the template matched must survive the rewrite.
events.behavior: Block a write that lands outside the Bootcamper's project (INV-200) or that carries a secret (INV-109).

kiroMechanism.notes: Direct equivalent with a matcher rewritten to Kiro's write-tool names by the tool-names substitution set; exit 2 blocks the tool call. The matcher above is authored in the template's tool vocabulary and carries the Kiro regex only once the contract has been applied — see assumptionDependentValues. The matcher name set is assumption A3, verified by Test_Checklist step 11.

portedProseLocations.note: Design-declared Tier 1 placement in ported prose.

events.residualGap: Without the Tier 2 install the gate is advisory: the rules hold as instructions, but nothing mechanically blocks an offending write.

events.behavior: Require every response that expects an answer to end with exactly one closing 👉 question, and never a second.

kiroMechanism.notes: Kiro has a Stop trigger but documents blocking only for PreToolUse, UserPromptSubmit, and PreTaskExec, so the installed hook can advise but not enforce.

portedProseLocations.note: Design-declared Tier 1 placement: ground rules plus each module's close phase.

parityGap.description: The template hook blocks a response that omits the closing 👉 question. Kiro's Stop trigger cannot block, so the rule is advisory at every tier.
parityGap.mitigation: The rule is stated as an instruction in the Tier 1 ground rules, and the installed Stop hook still nudges. The template biased this hook toward silence because duplicate closing questions are the top complaint, so an advisory-only version fails in the safe direction.

events.residualGap: Enforcement is advisory at every tier, including Tier 2.

events.behavior: Fold the recap checkpoint into the durable recap before context compaction discards the material it is built from.

kiroMechanism.notes: Kiro provides no PreCompact trigger. No hook definition exists for this behavior at any tier.

portedProseLocations.note: Design-declared Tier 1 placement: module close phase and the graduation recap.

parityGap.description: Folding is not guaranteed at the exact pre-compaction moment, because nothing fires there.
parityGap.mitigation: The per-turn UserPromptSubmit checkpoint tick keeps the checkpoint at most one turn behind and guarantees the checkpoint file exists, and the Tier 1 instruction folds at module close, at graduation, and at session close-out. Worst-case loss is one turn of unfolded recap material.

events.residualGap: Timing, not content: folding happens at declared boundaries rather than immediately before compaction.

events.behavior: On session end, stop any container the bootcamp started — stop, never remove (INV-101) — and perform a final recap fold.

kiroMechanism.notes: Kiro provides no SessionEnd trigger. No hook definition exists for this behavior at any tier.

portedProseLocations.note: Design-declared Tier 1 placement: ground rules plus the module that starts the container.

parityGap.description: Nothing fires when a Kiro session ends, so container stop and the final fold cannot be automatic.
parityGap.mitigation: Both become explicit close-out steps the agent performs at every point it controls — Bootcamper says they are stopping, module close, and before a long pause — with INV-101's stop-never-remove rule stated in the Tier 1 ground rules. An abrupt end leaves the container running rather than removed, which is the recoverable direction.

events.residualGap: An abrupt session end performs no close-out; the container stays running and the per-turn checkpoint is the recovery point.
